Now — the mktemp fix. Design:

```sh
mkdir -p "$FAH_CONFIG_DIR"
FAH_TMP_CONF=$(mktemp "$FAH_CONFIG_DIR/.config.yaml.XXXXXX")
```

Considerations:
- busybox mktemp: supports `mktemp [-d] [-q] [-t] [-p DIR] [TEMPLATE]` — template form works (needs at least 6 X's? busybox requires the XXX suffix present in template; `.config.yaml.XXXXXX` has 6 X's at the end — good).
- dash on Ubuntu uses GNU coreutils mktemp — fine.
- macOS bash leg: BSD mktemp supports template args — fine.
- Failure handling: under `set -eu`, if mktemp fails, the script aborts — FAH_TMP_CONF stays "" and the trap `rm -f ""` is a no-op. Good.
- `mv -f` over `FAH_CONFIG_FILE` — mktemp creates with 0600 perms, mv preserves them → config.yaml gets 0600 instead of 0644. Acceptable, no secrets inside anyway. Worth a comment noting it.
- The trap cleanup still works: `rm -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF"`.
- `FAH_TMP_CONF=""` reset after mv still fine.

Wait — one subtlety: `mv -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF" "$FAH_CONFIG_FILE"` when target exists on a different... no, same dir. Fine.

Another subtlety: with `> "$FAH_TMP_CONF"` the file was created at redirect time and truncated. With mktemp, the file exists (empty) before the `{ ... } > "$FAH_TMP_CONF"` block — the redirect truncates it. Same result.

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1555 (W1, lazy/windowed-everywhere reads): the legacy full-open call
  sites migrate to windowed opens, so a session ledger past the gh-1073
  2 GiB full-open backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path.
  The TUI session picker, `/resume`, and the boot name-resolution scan
  open windowed and resolve the display name through paged reads; the
  subagent transcript preview opens the child windowed (tail only); the
  `_loadSession` marathon fallback no longer degenerates to a refused
  full open when the boundary walk exhausts its page cap (it proceeds
  with the tail-anchored windowed session; the boot cap owns over-window
  residue); and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver opens windowed,
  reading the whole ledger for the cost/inspect views through the new
  `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident` — a sequential forward scan in
  bounded strips (`WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder`), not the
  boundary-walk's doubling strips (whose per-strip record cap measured
  ~13x read/parse amplification over the whole file). The same change
  block-prepends paged chunks in `_indexChunk` (one `insertAll` per
  list), removing an O(n²) the suspended-eviction walk paid per record.
  Trajectory export streaming (AC3a), split-and-retain rotation
  activation (W2), and the opt-in write-side caps (W3) remain follow-up
  work.

- gh-1605: the FinalizeGate gains a "grader parity" named check. A
  produced entry point (script/CLI the verifier will run itself) is only
  verified when it survives the grader's own invocation: the checklist
  must re-run each produced entry point from a different working
===

54:- gh-1603: unattended runs can no longer end as a clean success on empty

The CHANGELOG has `## Unreleased` with entries like `- gh-1605: ...`. I'll add a `- gh-1596: ...` entry at the top of Unreleased (newest first, gh-1555 is on top now — hmm, gh-1555 on top, then gh-1605, then gh-1603. Order isn't strictly numeric. gh-1555's entry was added by the just-merged commit. I'll add mine on top since it's the newest change).

Now — the mktemp fix. Design:

```sh
mkdir -p "$FAH_CONFIG_DIR"
FAH_TMP_CONF=$(mktemp "$FAH_CONFIG_DIR/.config.yaml.XXXXXX")
```

Considerations:
- busybox mktemp: supports `mktemp [-d] [-q] [-t] [-p DIR] [TEMPLATE]` — template form works (needs at least 6 X's? busybox requires the XXX suffix present in template; `.config.yaml.XXXXXX` has 6 X's at the end — good).
- dash on Ubuntu uses GNU coreutils mktemp — fine.
- macOS bash leg: BSD mktemp supports template args — fine.
- Failure handling: under `set -eu`, if mktemp fails, the script aborts — FAH_TMP_CONF stays "" and the trap `rm -f ""` is a no-op. Good.
- `mv -f` over `FAH_CONFIG_FILE` — mktemp creates with 0600 perms, mv preserves them → config.yaml gets 0600 instead of 0644. Acceptable, no secrets inside anyway. Worth a comment noting it.
- The trap cleanup still works: `rm -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF"`.
- `FAH_TMP_CONF=""` reset after mv still fine.

Wait — one subtlety: `mv -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF" "$FAH_CONFIG_FILE"` when target exists on a different... no, same dir. Fine.

Another subtlety: with `> "$FAH_TMP_CONF"` the file was created at redirect time and truncated. With mktemp, the file exists (empty) before the `{ ... } > "$FAH_TMP_CONF"` block — the redirect truncates it. Same result.

Now — TDD for mktemp (Thread 5). RED test: assert the emitted POSIX artifacts don't use a predictable fixed temp path — i.e. scan for `.config.yaml.tmp` (fixed name) and/or require `mktemp` for temp files in the template. Thread 4 (AC3 note) — documentation in PR description; I'll check if dmtools can update the PR body. Let me check dmtools capabilities. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# setup.sh — interactive configuration wizard for the Fa CLI.
#              Run this after `install.sh` to pick a provider, model, API key,
#              mode and approval policy.
#
#                curl -fsSL "https://fa1.dev/setup.sh" | sh
#
# What it does:
#   1. Verifies `fa` is installed.
#   2. Interactively picks a provider + model (or a custom endpoint).
#   3. Collects the API key and writes ~/.fah/config.yaml.
#   4. Optionally persists the API key in your shell startup file.
#
# {{GENERATED_HEADER}}

# gh-1596: this script runs under `curl | sh` — the shebang is dead text and
# whatever `sh` resolves to executes it. POSIX sh only (dash + busybox ash +
# bash): no `printf -v`, no `[[`, no arrays, no `read -p/-a/-N`, no
# `${var,,}`, no `=~`. UT-1 (test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart) lints
# the dialect; UT-2 pins the regenerated bytes.

set -eu  # no pipefail: dash (Ubuntu sh) lacks it

# E4: an unset HOME would die later inside the config path with a bare
# "parameter not set" — fail here, clearly, before anything else runs.
if [ -z "${HOME:-}" ]; then
  printf '\033[1;31m✘\033[0m %s\n' '$HOME is not set — cannot write the Fa config. Set HOME and re-run.' >&2

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1555 (W1, lazy/windowed-everywhere reads): the legacy full-open call
  sites migrate to windowed opens, so a session ledger past the gh-1073
  2 GiB full-open backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path.
  The TUI session picker, `/resume`, and the boot name-resolution scan
  open windowed and resolve the display name through paged reads; the
  subagent transcript preview opens the child windowed (tail only); the
  `_loadSession` marathon fallback no longer degenerates to a refused
  full open when the boundary walk exhausts its page cap (it proceeds
  with the tail-anchored windowed session; the boot cap owns over-window
  residue); and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver opens windowed,
  reading the whole ledger for the cost/inspect views through the new
  `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident` — a sequential forward scan in
  bounded strips (`WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder`), not the
  boundary-walk's doubling strips (whose per-strip record cap measured
  ~13x read/parse amplification over the whole file). The same change
  block-prepends paged chunks in `_indexChunk` (one `insertAll` per
  list), removing an O(n²) the suspended-eviction walk paid per record.
  Trajectory export streaming (AC3a), split-and-retain rotation
  activation (W2), and the opt-in write-side caps (W3) remain follow-up
  work.

- gh-1605: the FinalizeGate gains a "grader parity" named check. A
  produced entry point (script/CLI the verifier will run itself) is only
  verified when it survives the grader's own invocation: the checklist
  must re-run each produced entry point from a different working
===

54:- gh-1603: unattended runs can no longer end as a clean success on empty

The CHANGELOG has `## Unreleased` with entries like `- gh-1605: ...`. I'll add a `- gh-1596: ...` entry at the top of Unreleased (newest first, gh-1555 is on top now — hmm, gh-1555 on top, then gh-1605, then gh-1603. Order isn't strictly numeric. gh-1555's entry was added by the just-merged commit. I'll add mine on top since it's the newest change).

Now — the mktemp fix. Design:

```sh
mkdir -p "$FAH_CONFIG_DIR"
FAH_TMP_CONF=$(mktemp "$FAH_CONFIG_DIR/.config.yaml.XXXXXX")
```

Considerations:
- busybox mktemp: supports `mktemp [-d] [-q] [-t] [-p DIR] [TEMPLATE]` — template form works (needs at least 6 X's? busybox requires the XXX suffix present in template; `.config.yaml.XXXXXX` has 6 X's at the end — good).
- dash on Ubuntu uses GNU coreutils mktemp — fine.
- macOS bash leg: BSD mktemp supports template args — fine.
- Failure handling: under `set -eu`, if mktemp fails, the script aborts — FAH_TMP_CONF stays "" and the trap `rm -f ""` is a no-op. Good.
- `mv -f` over `FAH_CONFIG_FILE` — mktemp creates with 0600 perms, mv preserves them → config.yaml gets 0600 instead of 0644. Acceptable, no secrets inside anyway. Worth a comment noting it.
- The trap cleanup still works: `rm -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF"`.
- `FAH_TMP_CONF=""` reset after mv still fine.

Wait — one subtlety: `mv -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF" "$FAH_CONFIG_FILE"` when target exists on a different... no, same dir. Fine.

Another subtlety: with `> "$FAH_TMP_CONF"` the file was created at redirect time and truncated. With mktemp, the file exists (empty) before the `{ ... } > "$FAH_TMP_CONF"` block — the redirect truncates it. Same result.

Now — TDD for mktemp (Thread 5). RED test: assert the emitted POSIX artifacts don't use a predictable fixed temp path — i.e. scan for `.config.yaml.tmp` (fixed name) and/or require `mktemp` for temp files in the template. For Thread 1 (comment fix) — no behavior change, doc only. The TDD rule says never change production code without a reproducing test — these are comments (no production behavior). The golden test already covers regeneration consistency.

Thread 4 (AC3 note) — documentation in PR description; I'll check if dmtools can update the PR body. Let me check dmtools capabilities. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# setup.sh — interactive configuration wizard for the Fa CLI.
#              Run this after `install.sh` to pick a provider, model, API key,
#              mode and approval policy.
#
#                curl -fsSL "https://fa1.dev/setup.sh" | sh
#
# What it does:
#   1. Verifies `fa` is installed.
#   2. Interactively picks a provider + model (or a custom endpoint).
#   3. Collects the API key and writes ~/.fah/config.yaml.
#   4. Optionally persists the API key in your shell startup file.
#
# {{GENERATED_HEADER}}

# gh-1596: this script runs under `curl | sh` — the shebang is dead text and
# whatever `sh` resolves to executes it. POSIX sh only (dash + busybox ash +
# bash): no `printf -v`, no `[[`, no arrays, no `read -p/-a/-N`, no
# `${var,,}`, no `=~`. UT-1 (test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart) lints
# the dialect; UT-2 pins the regenerated bytes.

set -eu  # no pipefail: dash (Ubuntu sh) lacks it

# E4: an unset HOME would die later inside the config path with a bare
# "parameter not set" — fail here, clearly, before anything else runs.
if [ -z "${HOME:-}" ]; then
  printf '\033[1;31m✘\033[0m %s\n' '$HOME is not set — cannot write the Fa config. Set HOME and re-run.' >&2
  exit 1
fi

FAH_CONFIG_DIR="$HOME/.fah"
FAH_CONFIG_FILE="$FAH_CONFIG_DIR/config.yaml"
FAH_TMP_CONF=""  # config write is atomic (tmp + mv); cleaned on any exit
FAH_STTY_SAVED=""  # termios during hidden reads; restored on any exit

trap 'rm -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF"
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi' EXIT

# ── TTY handling ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if [ -t 0 ]; then
  FAH_TTY="/dev/stdin"
else
  FAH_TTY="/dev/tty"
fi

# ── Output helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
say() {
  printf '%s\n' "$*"
}

info() {
  printf '\033[1;34m→\033[0m %s\n' "$*"
}

ok() {
  printf '\033[1;32m✔\033[0m %s\n' "$*"
}

#1596
### What changed
- Rebuilt the first-run wizard (`site/setup.sh`) as generator-rendered POSIX sh: `scripts/gen_installers.dart` now emits the provider/mode/approval menus from the live catalog, and the template dropped every bashism (`printf -v`, `read -p`, `read -s`) that crashed dash and silently corrupted busybox ash under `curl | sh` (#1596).
- New REG CI leg `installer-portability` (path-triggered on `site/**` + the generator): ubuntu runs dash + busybox ash, macOS runs bash; red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class.

### Key decisions
- Single source of truth: the `/model` TUI presets table (`lib/src/cli/model_presets.dart`, extracted from `provider_models.dart`) now feeds both the CLI menu and the installer menus — the provider/approval data no longer has a second copy in `install-config.yaml`.
- Hidden key entry uses `stty -echo` + by-name `read` (dash has no `read -s`); the key never rides `printf` argv (ps-safe) and is byte-scanned out of every test transcript.
- EOF/Ctrl-C mid-wizard aborts non-zero under `set -eu` — never a half-written `~/.fah`; non-TTY runs print guidance and exit 1.
- Shell-less hosts SKIP their IT cases with named reasons; the CI job installs dash + busybox on ubuntu first (skip-not-fail, macOS pays nothing for dash).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart test/site/installer_golden_test.dart
dart test test/integration/setup_wizard_portability_test.dart   # --tags integration
# live, on a terminal:
dash -c 'cat site/setup.sh | dash'
```

> Note: a bare full-suite run on a dev box shows failures in files this PR
> does not touch, all environment-shaped and reproduced on `origin/main`:
> `test/browser_ext/*` needs Chrome for Testing (CI runs them only in
> browser-ext.yml); the `headless_*` / `backend_mode` / `yolo_rm_*` CLI
> integration tests fail when the harness's own `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` /
> `FA_PROVIDER_*` env leaks into the spawned CLI (they pass with those vars
> unset); `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts in the pty2
> native layer at VM teardown after its 5 tests pass.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CAT[model_presets.dart — live catalog] --> GEN[gen_installers.dart]
  GEN --> T[setup.sh.template — POSIX sh]
  T --> S[site/setup.sh — golden-pinned bytes]
  S -->|curl | sh| DASH[dash / busybox ash / bash — pty IT]
  CI[installer-portability CI leg] -->|red| BLOCK[quality gate blocks merge]
```

</details>

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1555 (W1, lazy/windowed-everywhere reads): the legacy full-open call
  sites migrate to windowed opens, so a session ledger past the gh-1073
  2 GiB full-open backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path.
  The TUI session picker, `/resume`, and the boot name-resolution scan
  open windowed and resolve the display name through paged reads; the
  subagent transcript preview opens the child windowed (tail only); the
  `_loadSession` marathon fallback no longer degenerates to a refused
  full open when the boundary walk exhausts its page cap (it proceeds
  with the tail-anchored windowed session; the boot cap owns over-window
  residue); and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver opens windowed,
  reading the whole ledger for the cost/inspect views through the new
  `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident` — a sequential forward scan in
  bounded strips (`WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder`), not the
  boundary-walk's doubling strips (whose per-strip record cap measured
  ~13x read/parse amplification over the whole file). The same change
  block-prepends paged chunks in `_indexChunk` (one `insertAll` per
  list), removing an O(n²) the suspended-eviction walk paid per record.
  Trajectory export streaming (AC3a), split-and-retain rotation
  activation (W2), and the opt-in write-side caps (W3) remain follow-up
  work.

- gh-1605: the FinalizeGate gains a "grader parity" named check. A
  produced entry point (script/CLI the verifier will run itself) is only
  verified when it survives the grader's own invocation: the checklist
  must re-run each produced entry point from a different working

Order isn't strictly numeric. gh-1555's entry was added by the just-merged commit. I'll add mine on top since it's the newest change).

Now — the mktemp fix. Design:

```sh
mkdir -p "$FAH_CONFIG_DIR"
FAH_TMP_CONF=$(mktemp "$FAH_CONFIG_DIR/.config.yaml.XXXXXX")
```

Considerations:
- busybox mktemp: supports `mktemp [-d] [-q] [-t] [-p DIR] [TEMPLATE]` — template form works (needs at least 6 X's? busybox requires the XXX suffix present in template; `.config.yaml.XXXXXX` has 6 X's at the end — good).
- dash on Ubuntu uses GNU coreutils mktemp — fine.
- macOS bash leg: BSD mktemp supports template args — fine.
- Failure handling: under `set -eu`, if mktemp fails, the script aborts — FAH_TMP_CONF stays "" and the trap `rm -f ""` is a no-op. Good.
- `mv -f` over `FAH_CONFIG_FILE` — mktemp creates with 0600 perms, mv preserves them → config.yaml gets 0600 instead of 0644. Acceptable, no secrets inside anyway. Worth a comment noting it.
- The trap cleanup still works: `rm -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF"`.
- `FAH_TMP_CONF=""` reset after mv still fine.

Wait — one subtlety: `mv -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF" "$FAH_CONFIG_FILE"` when target exists on a different... no, same dir. Fine.

Another subtlety: with `> "$FAH_TMP_CONF"` the file was created at redirect time and truncated. With mktemp, the file exists (empty) before the `{ ... } > "$FAH_TMP_CONF"` block — the redirect truncates it. Same result.

Now — TDD for mktemp (Thread 5). RED test: assert the emitted POSIX artifacts don't use a predictable fixed temp path — i.e. scan for `.config.yaml.tmp` (fixed name) and/or require `mktemp` for temp files in the template. RED first: currently `.config.yaml.tmp` is present → test fails. Then fix template, regenerate → green.

Also verify the generated golden updates — installer_golden_test compares committed vs freshly rendered; after regenerating site/setup.sh it passes.

For Thread 1 (comment fix) — no behavior change, doc only. The TDD rule says never change production code without a reproducing test — these are comments (no production behavior). The golden test already covers regeneration consistency.

Thread 3 (format) — cosmetic, no tests needed beyond the suite.

Thread 4 (AC3 note) — documentation in PR description; I'll check if dmtools can update the PR body. Let me check dmtools capabilities. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# setup.sh — interactive configuration wizard for the Fa CLI.
#              Run this after `install.sh` to pick a provider, model, API key,
#              mode and approval policy.
#
#                curl -fsSL "https://fa1.dev/setup.sh" | sh
#
# What it does:
#   1. Verifies `fa` is installed.
#   2. Interactively picks a provider + model (or a custom endpoint).
#   3. Collects the API key and writes ~/.fah/config.yaml.
#   4. Optionally persists the API key in your shell startup file.
#
# {{GENERATED_HEADER}}

# gh-1596: this script runs under `curl | sh` — the shebang is dead text and
# whatever `sh` resolves to executes it. POSIX sh only (dash + busybox ash +
# bash): no `printf -v`, no `[[`, no arrays, no `read -p/-a/-N`, no
# `${var,,}`, no `=~`. UT-1 (test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart) lints
# the dialect; UT-2 pins the regenerated bytes.

set -eu  # no pipefail: dash (Ubuntu sh) lacks it

# E4: an unset HOME would die later inside the config path with a bare
# "parameter not set" — fail here, clearly, before anything else runs.
if [ -z "${HOME:-}" ]; then
  printf '\033[1;31m✘\033[0m %s\n' '$HOME is not set — cannot write the Fa config. Set HOME and re-run.' >&2
  exit 1
fi

FAH_CONFIG_DIR="$HOME/.fah"
FAH_CONFIG_FILE="$FAH_CONFIG_DIR/config.yaml"
FAH_TMP_CONF=""  # config write is atomic (tmp + mv); cleaned on any exit
FAH_STTY_SAVED=""  # termios during hidden reads; restored on any exit

trap 'rm -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF"
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi' EXIT

# ── TTY handling ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if [ -t 0 ]; then
  FAH_TTY="/dev/stdin"
else
  FAH_TTY="/dev/tty"
fi

# ── Output helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
say() {
  printf '%s\n' "$*"
}

info() {
  printf '\033[1;34m→\033[0m %s\n' "$*"
}

ok() {
  printf '\033[1;32m✔\033[0m %s\n' "$*"
}

- Rebuilt the first-run wizard (`site/setup.sh`) as generator-rendered POSIX sh: `scripts/gen_installers.dart` now emits the provider/mode/approval menus from the live catalog, and the template dropped every bashism (`printf -v`, `read -p`, `read -s`) that crashed dash and silently corrupted busybox ash under `curl | sh` (#1596).
- New REG CI leg `installer-portability` (path-triggered on `site/**` + the generator): ubuntu runs dash + busybox ash, macOS runs bash; red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class.

### Key decisions
- Single source of truth: the `/model` TUI presets table (`lib/src/cli/model_presets.dart`, extracted from `provider_models.dart`) now feeds both the CLI menu and the installer menus — the provider/approval data no longer has a second copy in `install-config.yaml`.
- Hidden key entry uses `stty -echo` + by-name `read` (dash has no `read -s`); the key never rides `printf` argv (ps-safe) and is byte-scanned out of every test transcript.
- EOF/Ctrl-C mid-wizard aborts non-zero under `set -eu` — never a half-written `~/.fah`; non-TTY runs print guidance and exit 1.
- Shell-less hosts SKIP their IT cases with named reasons; the CI job installs dash + busybox on ubuntu first (skip-not-fail, macOS pays nothing for dash).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart test/site/installer_golden_test.dart
dart test test/integration/setup_wizard_portability_test.dart   # --tags integration
# live, on a terminal:
dash -c 'cat site/setup.sh | dash'
```

> Note: a bare full-suite run on a dev box shows failures in files this PR
> does not touch, all environment-shaped and reproduced on `origin/main`:
> `test/browser_ext/*` needs Chrome for Testing (CI runs them only in
> browser-ext.yml); the `headless_*` / `backend_mode` / `yolo_rm_*` CLI
> integration tests fail when the harness's own `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` /
> `FA_PROVIDER_*` env leaks into the spawned CLI (they pass with those vars
> unset); `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts in the pty2
> native layer at VM teardown after its 5 tests pass.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CAT[model_presets.dart — live catalog] --> GEN[gen_installers.dart]
  GEN --> T[setup.sh.template — POSIX sh]
  T --> S[site/setup.sh — golden-pinned bytes]
  S -->|curl | sh| DASH[dash / busybox ash / bash — pty IT]
  CI[installer-portability CI leg] -->|red| BLOCK[quality gate blocks merge]
```

</details>

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1555 (W1, lazy/windowed-everywhere reads): the legacy full-open call
  sites migrate to windowed opens, so a session ledger past the gh-1073
  2 GiB full-open backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path.
  The TUI session picker, `/resume`, and the boot name-resolution scan
  open windowed and resolve the display name through paged reads; the
  subagent transcript preview opens the child windowed (tail only); the
  `_loadSession` marathon fallback no longer degenerates to a refused
  full open when the boundary walk exhausts its page cap (it proceeds
  with the tail-anchored windowed session; the boot cap owns over-window
  residue); and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver opens windowed,
  reading the whole ledger for the cost/inspect views through the new
  `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident` — a sequential forward scan in
  bounded strips (`WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder`), not the
  boundary-walk's doubling strips (whose per-strip record cap measured
  ~13x read/parse amplification over the whole file). The same change
  block-prepends paged chunks in `_indexChunk` (one `insertAll` per
  list), removing an O(n²) the suspended-eviction walk paid per record.
  Trajectory export streaming (AC3a), split-and-retain rotation
  activation (W2), and the opt-in write-side caps (W3) remain follow-up
  work.

- gh-1605: the FinalizeGate gains a "grader parity" named check. A
  produced entry point (script/CLI the verifier will run itself) is only
  verified when it survives the grader's own invocation: the checklist
  must re-run each produced entry point from a different working

Now — the mktemp fix. Design:

```sh
mkdir -p "$FAH_CONFIG_DIR"
FAH_TMP_CONF=$(mktemp "$FAH_CONFIG_DIR/.config.yaml.XXXXXX")
```

Considerations:
- busybox mktemp: supports `mktemp [-d] [-q] [-t] [-p DIR] [TEMPLATE]` — template form works (needs at least 6 X's? busybox requires the XXX suffix present in template; `.config.yaml.XXXXXX` has 6 X's at the end — good).
- dash on Ubuntu uses GNU coreutils mktemp — fine.
- macOS bash leg: BSD mktemp supports template args — fine.
- Failure handling: under `set -eu`, if mktemp fails, the script aborts — FAH_TMP_CONF stays "" and the trap `rm -f ""` is a no-op. Good.
- `mv -f` over `FAH_CONFIG_FILE` — mktemp creates with 0600 perms, mv preserves them → config.yaml gets 0600 instead of 0644. Acceptable, no secrets inside anyway. Worth a comment noting it.
- The trap cleanup still works: `rm -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF"`.
- `FAH_TMP_CONF=""` reset after mv still fine.

Wait — one subtlety: `mv -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF" "$FAH_CONFIG_FILE"` when target exists on a different... no, same dir. Fine.

Another subtlety: with `> "$FAH_TMP_CONF"` the file was created at redirect time and truncated. With mktemp, the file exists (empty) before the `{ ... } > "$FAH_TMP_CONF"` block — the redirect truncates it. Same result.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# setup.sh — interactive configuration wizard for the Fa CLI.
#              Run this after `install.sh` to pick a provider, model, API key,
#              mode and approval policy.
#
#                curl -fsSL "https://fa1.dev/setup.sh" | sh
#
# What it does:
#   1. Verifies `fa` is installed.
#   2. Interactively picks a provider + model (or a custom endpoint).
#   3. Collects the API key and writes ~/.fah/config.yaml.
#   4. Optionally persists the API key in your shell startup file.
#
# {{GENERATED_HEADER}}

# gh-1596: this script runs under `curl | sh` — the shebang is dead text and
# whatever `sh` resolves to executes it. POSIX sh only (dash + busybox ash +
# bash): no `printf -v`, no `[[`, no arrays, no `read -p/-a/-N`, no
# `${var,,}`, no `=~`. UT-1 (test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart) lints
# the dialect; UT-2 pins the regenerated bytes.

set -eu  # no pipefail: dash (Ubuntu sh) lacks it

# E4: an unset HOME would die later inside the config path with a bare
# "parameter not set" — fail here, clearly, before anything else runs.
if [ -z "${HOME:-}" ]; then
  printf '\033[1;31m✘\033[0m %s\n' '$HOME is not set — cannot write the Fa config. Set HOME and re-run.' >&2
  exit 1
fi

FAH_CONFIG_DIR="$HOME/.fah"
FAH_CONFIG_FILE="$FAH_CONFIG_DIR/config.yaml"
FAH_TMP_CONF=""  # config write is atomic (tmp + mv); cleaned on any exit
FAH_STTY_SAVED=""  # termios during hidden reads; restored on any exit

trap 'rm -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF"
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi' EXIT

# ── TTY handling ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if [ -t 0 ]; then
  FAH_TTY="/dev/stdin"
else
  FAH_TTY="/dev/tty"
fi

# ── Output helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
say() {
  printf '%s\n' "$*"
}

info() {
  printf '\033[1;34m→\033[0m %s\n' "$*"
}

ok() {
  printf '\033[1;32m✔\033[0m %s\n' "$*"
}

`install.sh.template` already uses `mktemp` (with fallback `mktemp -t`) — good precedent in the codebase. The setup wizard is the only artifact with a fixed temp name.

Note: install.sh uses `mktemp 2>/dev/null || mktemp -t fa-archive` — for maximum portability (BSD mktemp without template works; GNU works; busybox `mktemp` alone works too; `mktemp -t` is deprecated on GNU but works). For the setup wizard inside `$FAH_CONFIG_DIR` we specifically want the file IN that directory (same-filesystem atomic mv + cleanup), so `mktemp "$FAH_CONFIG_DIR/.config.yaml.XXXXXX"` (template form) is right, matching the reviewer's exact suggestion.

Edge: if mktemp fails (set -eu) → abort. Fine; trap cleanup of "" is no-op.

Now the REST of the template's write block:

```sh
mkdir -p "$FAH_CONFIG_DIR"
FAH_TMP_CONF="$FAH_CONFIG_DIR/.config.yaml.tmp"
{
  printf ...
} > "$FAH_TMP_CONF"
mv -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF" "$FAH_CONFIG_FILE"
FAH_TMP_CONF=""
```

becomes:

```sh
mkdir -p "$FAH_CONFIG_DIR"
# mktemp, not a fixed name: a predictable path is symlink-followable — a
# pre-planted `$FAH_CONFIG_DIR/.config.yaml.tmp` link would redirect the
# write (review hardening, gh-1596). The XXX suffix is required by
# mktemp (GNU + busybox + BSD all take the template form); mktemp creates
# the file 0600, so the config lands owner-only.
FAH_TMP_CONF=$(mktemp "$FAH_CONFIG_DIR/.config.yaml.XXXXXX")
{
  printf ...
} > "$FAH_TMP_CONF"
mv -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF" "$FAH_CONFIG_FILE"
FAH_TMP_CONF=""
```

Hmm wait — comment style: `_stripCommentLines` blanks full-line comments before linting, so comments are free text (but avoid forbidden constructs in comment text? No — comments are stripped entirely line-wise when trimmed line starts with '#'). Careful: `$_` style things in comments are fine.

One nuance — `mv -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF" "$FAH_CONFIG_FILE"`: mktemp file perms 0600 → config.yaml becomes 0600. The integration test may check content only. Fine. Should I chmod 644? The old behavior produced umask-default perms (usually 644). Since config.yaml is key-free, 644 vs 600 doesn't matter functionally; 600 is strictly safer. But would anything in the harness read config.yaml as another user? No. Keep 0600, mention in comment.

#1596
### What changed
- Rebuilt the first-run wizard (`site/setup.sh`) as generator-rendered POSIX sh: `scripts/gen_installers.dart` now emits the provider/mode/approval menus from the live catalog, and the template dropped every bashism (`printf -v`, `read -p`, `read -s`) that crashed dash and silently corrupted busybox ash under `curl | sh` (#1596).
- New REG CI leg `installer-portability` (path-triggered on `site/**` + the generator): ubuntu runs dash + busybox ash, macOS runs bash; red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class.

### Key decisions
- Single source of truth: the `/model` TUI presets table (`lib/src/cli/model_presets.dart`, extracted from `provider_models.dart`) now feeds both the CLI menu and the installer menus — the provider/approval data no longer has a second copy in `install-config.yaml`.
- Hidden key entry uses `stty -echo` + by-name `read` (dash has no `read -s`); the key never rides `printf` argv (ps-safe) and is byte-scanned out of every test transcript.
- EOF/Ctrl-C mid-wizard aborts non-zero under `set -eu` — never a half-written `~/.fah`; non-TTY runs print guidance and exit 1.
- Shell-less hosts SKIP their IT cases with named reasons; the CI job installs dash + busybox on ubuntu first (skip-not-fail, macOS pays nothing for dash).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart test/site/installer_golden_test.dart
dart test test/integration/setup_wizard_portability_test.dart   # --tags integration
# live, on a terminal:
dash -c 'cat site/setup.sh | dash'
```

> Note: a bare full-suite run on a dev box shows failures in files this PR
> does not touch, all environment-shaped and reproduced on `origin/main`:
> `test/browser_ext/*` needs Chrome for Testing (CI runs them only in
> browser-ext.yml); the `headless_*` / `backend_mode` / `yolo_rm_*` CLI
> integration tests fail when the harness's own `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` /
> `FA_PROVIDER_*` env leaks into the spawned CLI (they pass with those vars
> unset); `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts in the pty2
> native layer at VM teardown after its 5 tests pass.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CAT[model_presets.dart — live catalog] --> GEN[gen_installers.dart]
  GEN --> T[setup.sh.template — POSIX sh]
  T --> S[site/setup.sh — golden-pinned bytes]
  S -->|curl | sh| DASH[dash / busybox ash / bash — pty IT]
  CI[installer-portability CI leg] -->|red| BLOCK[quality gate blocks merge]
```

</details>

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1555 (W1, lazy/windowed-everywhere reads): the legacy full-open call
  sites migrate to windowed opens, so a session ledger past the gh-1073
  2 GiB full-open backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path.
  The TUI session picker, `/resume`, and the boot name-resolution scan
  open windowed and resolve the display name through paged reads; the
  subagent transcript preview opens the child windowed (tail only); the
  `_loadSession` marathon fallback no longer degenerates to a refused
  full open when the boundary walk exhausts its page cap (it proceeds
  with the tail-anchored windowed session; the boot cap owns over-window
  residue); and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver opens windowed,
  reading the whole ledger for the cost/inspect views through the new
  `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident` — a sequential forward scan in
  bounded strips (`WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder`), not the
  boundary-walk's doubling strips (whose per-strip record cap measured
  ~13x read/parse amplification over the whole file). The same change
  block-prepends paged chunks in `_indexChunk` (one `insertAll` per
  list), removing an O(n²) the suspended-eviction walk paid per record.
  Trajectory export streaming (AC3a), split-and-retain rotation
  activation (W2), and the opt-in write-side caps (W3) remain follow-up
  work.

  verified when it survives the grader's own invocation: the checklist

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# setup.sh — interactive configuration wizard for the Fa CLI.
#              Run this after `install.sh` to pick a provider, model, API key,
#              mode and approval policy.
#
#                curl -fsSL "https://fa1.dev/setup.sh" | sh
#
# What it does:
#   1. Verifies `fa` is installed.
#   2. Interactively picks a provider + model (or a custom endpoint).
#   3. Collects the API key and writes ~/.fah/config.yaml.
#   4. Optionally persists the API key in your shell startup file.
#
# {{GENERATED_HEADER}}

# gh-1596: this script runs under `curl | sh` — the shebang is dead text and
# whatever `sh` resolves to executes it. POSIX sh only (dash + busybox ash +
# bash): no `printf -v`, no `[[`, no arrays, no `read -p/-a/-N`, no
# `${var,,}`, no `=~`. UT-1 (test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart) lints
# the dialect; UT-2 pins the regenerated bytes.

set -eu  # no pipefail: dash (Ubuntu sh) lacks it

# E4: an unset HOME would die later inside the config path with a bare
# "parameter not set" — fail here, clearly, before anything else runs.
if [ -z "${HOME:-}" ]; then
  printf '\033[1;31m✘\033[0m %s\n' '$HOME is not set — cannot write the Fa config. Set HOME and re-run.' >&2
  exit 1
fi

FAH_CONFIG_DIR="$HOME/.fah"
FAH_CONFIG_FILE="$FAH_CONFIG_DIR/config.yaml"
FAH_TMP_CONF=""  # config write is atomic (tmp + mv); cleaned on any exit
FAH_STTY_SAVED=""  # termios during hidden reads; restored on any exit

trap 'rm -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF"
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi' EXIT

# ── TTY handling ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if [ -t 0 ]; then
  FAH_TTY="/dev/stdin"
else
  FAH_TTY="/dev/tty"
fi

# ── Output helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
say() {
  printf '%s\n' "$*"
}

info() {
  printf '\033[1;34m→\033[0m %s\n' "$*"
}

ok() {
  printf '\033[1;32m✔\033[0m %s\n' "$*"
}

#1596
### What changed
- Rebuilt the first-run wizard (`site/setup.sh`) as generator-rendered POSIX sh: `scripts/gen_installers.dart` now emits the provider/mode/approval menus from the live catalog, and the template dropped every bashism (`printf -v`, `read -p`, `read -s`) that crashed dash and silently corrupted busybox ash under `curl | sh` (#1596).
- New REG CI leg `installer-portability` (path-triggered on `site/**` + the generator): ubuntu runs dash + busybox ash, macOS runs bash; red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class.

### Key decisions
- Single source of truth: the `/model` TUI presets table (`lib/src/cli/model_presets.dart`, extracted from `provider_models.dart`) now feeds both the CLI menu and the installer menus — the provider/approval data no longer has a second copy in `install-config.yaml`.
- Hidden key entry uses `stty -echo` + by-name `read` (dash has no `read -s`); the key never rides `printf` argv (ps-safe) and is byte-scanned out of every test transcript.
- EOF/Ctrl-C mid-wizard aborts non-zero under `set -eu` — never a half-written `~/.fah`; non-TTY runs print guidance and exit 1.
- Shell-less hosts SKIP their IT cases with named reasons; the CI job installs dash + busybox on ubuntu first (skip-not-fail, macOS pays nothing for dash).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart test/site/installer_golden_test.dart
dart test test/integration/setup_wizard_portability_test.dart   # --tags integration
# live, on a terminal:
dash -c 'cat site/setup.sh | dash'
```

> Note: a bare full-suite run on a dev box shows failures in files this PR
> does not touch, all environment-shaped and reproduced on `origin/main`:
> `test/browser_ext/*` needs Chrome for Testing (CI runs them only in
> browser-ext.yml); the `headless_*` / `backend_mode` / `yolo_rm_*` CLI
> integration tests fail when the harness's own `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` /
> `FA_PROVIDER_*` env leaks into the spawned CLI (they pass with those vars
> unset); `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts in the pty2
> native layer at VM teardown after its 5 tests pass.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CAT[model_presets.dart — live catalog] --> GEN[gen_installers.dart]
  GEN --> T[setup.sh.template — POSIX sh]
  T --> S[site/setup.sh — golden-pinned bytes]
  S -->|curl | sh| DASH[dash / busybox ash / bash — pty IT]
  CI[installer-portability CI leg] -->|red| BLOCK[quality gate blocks merge]
```

</details>

Now — the mktemp fix. Design:

```sh
mkdir -p "$FAH_CONFIG_DIR"
FAH_TMP_CONF=$(mktemp "$FAH_CONFIG_DIR/.config.yaml.XXXXXX")
```

Considerations:
- busybox mktemp: supports `mktemp [-d] [-q] [-t] [-p DIR] [TEMPLATE]` — template form works (needs at least 6 X's? busybox requires the XXX suffix present in template; `.config.yaml.XXXXXX` has 6 X's at the end — good).
- dash on Ubuntu uses GNU coreutils mktemp — fine.
- macOS bash leg: BSD mktemp supports template args — fine.
- Failure handling: under `set -eu`, if mktemp fails, the script aborts — FAH_TMP_CONF stays "" and the trap `rm -f ""` is a no-op. Good.
- `mv -f` over `FAH_CONFIG_FILE` — mktemp creates with 0600 perms, mv preserves them → config.yaml gets 0600 instead of 0644. Acceptable, no secrets inside anyway. Worth a comment noting it.
- The trap cleanup still works: `rm -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF"`.
- `FAH_TMP_CONF=""` reset after mv still fine.

Wait — one subtlety: `mv -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF" "$FAH_CONFIG_FILE"` when target exists on a different... no, same dir. Fine.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# setup.sh — interactive configuration wizard for the Fa CLI.
#              Run this after `install.sh` to pick a provider, model, API key,
#              mode and approval policy.
#
#                curl -fsSL "https://fa1.dev/setup.sh" | sh
#
# What it does:
#   1. Verifies `fa` is installed.
#   2. Interactively picks a provider + model (or a custom endpoint).
#   3. Collects the API key and writes ~/.fah/config.yaml.
#   4. Optionally persists the API key in your shell startup file.
#
# {{GENERATED_HEADER}}

# gh-1596: this script runs under `curl | sh` — the shebang is dead text and
# whatever `sh` resolves to executes it. POSIX sh only (dash + busybox ash +
# bash): no `printf -v`, no `[[`, no arrays, no `read -p/-a/-N`, no
# `${var,,}`, no `=~`. UT-1 (test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart) lints
# the dialect; UT-2 pins the regenerated bytes.

set -eu  # no pipefail: dash (Ubuntu sh) lacks it

# E4: an unset HOME would die later inside the config path with a bare

#1596
### What changed
- Rebuilt the first-run wizard (`site/setup.sh`) as generator-rendered POSIX sh: `scripts/gen_installers.dart` now emits the provider/mode/approval menus from the live catalog, and the template dropped every bashism (`printf -v`, `read -p`, `read -s`) that crashed dash and silently corrupted busybox ash under `curl | sh` (#1596).
- New REG CI leg `installer-portability` (path-triggered on `site/**` + the generator): ubuntu runs dash + busybox ash, macOS runs bash; red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class.

### Key decisions
- Single source of truth: the `/model` TUI presets table (`lib/src/cli/model_presets.dart`, extracted from `provider_models.dart`) now feeds both the CLI menu and the installer menus — the provider/approval data no longer has a second copy in `install-config.yaml`.
- Hidden key entry uses `stty -echo` + by-name `read` (dash has no `read -s`); the key never rides `printf` argv (ps-safe) and is byte-scanned out of every test transcript.
- EOF/Ctrl-C mid-wizard aborts non-zero under `set -eu` — never a half-written `~/.fah`; non-TTY runs print guidance and exit 1.
- Shell-less hosts SKIP their IT cases with named reasons; the CI job installs dash + busybox on ubuntu first (skip-not-fail, macOS pays nothing for dash).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart test/site/installer_golden_test.dart
dart test test/integration/setup_wizard_portability_test.dart   # --tags integration
# live, on a terminal:
dash -c 'cat site/setup.sh | dash'
```

> Note: a bare full-suite run on a dev box shows failures in files this PR
> does not touch, all environment-shaped and reproduced on `origin/main`:
> `test/browser_ext/*` needs Chrome for Testing (CI runs them only in
> browser-ext.yml); the `headless_*` / `backend_mode` / `yolo_rm_*` CLI
> integration tests fail when the harness's own `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` /
> `FA_PROVIDER_*` env leaks into the spawned CLI (they pass with those vars
> unset); `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts in the pty2
> native layer at VM teardown after its 5 tests pass.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CAT[model_presets.dart — live catalog] --> GEN[gen_installers.dart]
  GEN --> T[setup.sh.template — POSIX sh]
  T --> S[site/setup.sh — golden-pinned bytes]
  S -->|curl | sh| DASH[dash / busybox ash / bash — pty IT]
  CI[installer-portability CI leg] -->|red| BLOCK[quality gate blocks merge]
```

</details>

#1596
### What changed
- Rebuilt the first-run wizard (`site/setup.sh`) as generator-rendered POSIX sh: `scripts/gen_installers.dart` now emits the provider/mode/approval menus from the live catalog, and the template dropped every bashism (`printf -v`, `read -p`, `read -s`) that crashed dash and silently corrupted busybox ash under `curl | sh` (#1596).
- New REG CI leg `installer-portability` (path-triggered on `site/**` + the generator): ubuntu runs dash + busybox ash, macOS runs bash; red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class.

### Key decisions
- Single source of truth: the `/model` TUI presets table (`lib/src/cli/model_presets.dart`, extracted from `provider_models.dart`) now feeds both the CLI menu and the installer menus — the provider/approval data no longer has a second copy in `install-config.yaml`.
- Hidden key entry uses `stty -echo` + by-name `read` (dash has no `read -s`); the key never rides `printf` argv (ps-safe) and is byte-scanned out of every test transcript.
- EOF/Ctrl-C mid-wizard aborts non-zero under `set -eu` — never a half-written `~/.fah`; non-TTY runs print guidance and exit 1.
- Shell-less hosts SKIP their IT cases with named reasons; the CI job installs dash + busybox on ubuntu first (skip-not-fail, macOS pays nothing for dash).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart test/site/installer_golden_test.dart
dart test test/integration/setup_wizard_portability_test.dart   # --tags integration
# live, on a terminal:
dash -c 'cat site/setup.sh | dash'
```

> Note: a bare full-suite run on a dev box shows failures in files this PR
> does not touch, all environment-shaped and reproduced on `origin/main`:
> `test/browser_ext/*` needs Chrome for Testing (CI runs them only in
> browser-ext.yml); the `headless_*` / `backend_mode` / `yolo_rm_*` CLI
> integration tests fail when the harness's own `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` /
> `FA_PROVIDER_*` env leaks into the spawned CLI (they pass with those vars
> unset); `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts in the pty2
> native layer at VM teardown after its 5 tests pass.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CAT[model_presets.dart — live catalog] --> GEN[gen_installers.dart]
  GEN --> T[setup.sh.template — POSIX sh]
  T --> S[site/setup.sh — golden-pinned bytes]
  S -->|curl | sh| DASH[dash / busybox ash / bash — pty IT]
  CI[installer-portability CI leg] -->|red| BLOCK[quality gate blocks merge]
```

</details>

#1596
### What changed
- Rebuilt the first-run wizard (`site/setup.sh`) as generator-rendered POSIX sh: `scripts/gen_installers.dart` now emits the provider/mode/approval menus from the live catalog, and the template dropped every bashism (`printf -v`, `read -p`, `read -s`) that crashed dash and silently corrupted busybox ash under `curl | sh` (#1596).
- New REG CI leg `installer-portability` (path-triggered on `site/**` + the generator): ubuntu runs dash + busybox ash, macOS runs bash; red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class.

### Key decisions
- Single source of truth: the `/model` TUI presets table (`lib/src/cli/model_presets.dart`, extracted from `provider_models.dart`) now feeds both the CLI menu and the installer menus — the provider/approval data no longer has a second copy in `install-config.yaml`.
- Hidden key entry uses `stty -echo` + by-name `read` (dash has no `read -s`); the key never rides `printf` argv (ps-safe) and is byte-scanned out of every test transcript.
- EOF/Ctrl-C mid-wizard aborts non-zero under `set -eu` — never a half-written `~/.fah`; non-TTY runs print guidance and exit 1.
- Shell-less hosts SKIP their IT cases with named reasons; the CI job installs dash + busybox on ubuntu first (skip-not-fail, macOS pays nothing for dash).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart test/site/installer_golden_test.dart
dart test test/integration/setup_wizard_portability_test.dart   # --tags integration
# live, on a terminal:
dash -c 'cat site/setup.sh | dash'
```

> Note: a bare full-suite run on a dev box shows failures in files this PR
> does not touch, all environment-shaped and reproduced on `origin/main`:
> `test/browser_ext/*` needs Chrome for Testing (CI runs them only in
> browser-ext.yml); the `headless_*` / `backend_mode` / `yolo_rm_*` CLI
> integration tests fail when the harness's own `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` /
> `FA_PROVIDER_*` env leaks into the spawned CLI (they pass with those vars
> unset); `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts in the pty2
> native layer at VM teardown after its 5 tests pass.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CAT[model_presets.dart — live catalog] --> GEN[gen_installers.dart]
  GEN --> T[setup.sh.template — POSIX sh]
  T --> S[site/setup.sh — golden-pinned bytes]
  S -->|curl | sh| DASH[dash / busybox ash / bash — pty IT]
  CI[installer-portability CI leg] -->|red| BLOCK[quality gate blocks merge]
```

</details>

#1596
### What changed
- Rebuilt the first-run wizard (`site/setup.sh`) as generator-rendered POSIX sh: `scripts/gen_installers.dart` now emits the provider/mode/approval menus from the live catalog, and the template dropped every bashism (`printf -v`, `read -p`, `read -s`) that crashed dash and silently corrupted busybox ash under `curl | sh` (#1596).
- New REG CI leg `installer-portability` (path-triggered on `site/**` + the generator): ubuntu runs dash + busybox ash, macOS runs bash; red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class.

### Key decisions
- Single source of truth: the `/model` TUI presets table (`lib/src/cli/model_presets.dart`, extracted from `provider_models.dart`) now feeds both the CLI menu and the installer menus — the provider/approval data no longer has a second copy in `install-config.yaml`.
- Hidden key entry uses `stty -echo` + by-name `read` (dash has no `read -s`); the key never rides `printf` argv (ps-safe) and is byte-scanned out of every test transcript.
- EOF/Ctrl-C mid-wizard aborts non-zero under `set -eu` — never a half-written `~/.fah`; non-TTY runs print guidance and exit 1.
- Shell-less hosts SKIP their IT cases with named reasons; the CI job installs dash + busybox on ubuntu first (skip-not-fail, macOS pays nothing for dash).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart test/site/installer_golden_test.dart
dart test test/integration/setup_wizard_portability_test.dart   # --tags integration
# live, on a terminal:
dash -c 'cat site/setup.sh | dash'
```

> Note: a bare full-suite run on a dev box shows failures in files this PR
> does not touch, all environment-shaped and reproduced on `origin/main`:
> `test/browser_ext/*` needs Chrome for Testing (CI runs them only in
> browser-ext.yml); the `headless_*` / `backend_mode` / `yolo_rm_*` CLI
> integration tests fail when the harness's own `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` /
> `FA_PROVIDER_*` env leaks into the spawned CLI (they pass with those vars
> unset); `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts in the pty2
> native layer at VM teardown after its 5 tests pass.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CAT[model_presets.dart — live catalog] --> GEN[gen_installers.dart]
  GEN --> T[setup.sh.template — POSIX sh]
  T --> S[site/setup.sh — golden-pinned bytes]
  S -->|curl | sh| DASH[dash / busybox ash / bash — pty IT]
  CI[installer-portability CI leg] -->|red| BLOCK[quality gate blocks merge]
```

</details>

### What changed
- Rebuilt the first-run wizard (`site/setup.sh`) as generator-rendered POSIX sh: `scripts/gen_installers.dart` now emits the provider/mode/approval menus from the live catalog, and the template dropped every bashism (`printf -v`, `read -p`, `read -s`) that crashed dash and silently corrupted busybox ash under `curl | sh` (#1596).
- New REG CI leg `installer-portability` (path-triggered on `site/**` + the generator): ubuntu runs dash + busybox ash, macOS runs bash; red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class.

### Key decisions
- Single source of truth: the `/model` TUI presets table (`lib/src/cli/model_presets.dart`, extracted from `provider_models.dart`) now feeds both the CLI menu and the installer menus — the provider/approval data no longer has a second copy in `install-config.yaml`.
- Hidden key entry uses `stty -echo` + by-name `read` (dash has no `read -s`); the key never rides `printf` argv (ps-safe) and is byte-scanned out of every test transcript.
- EOF/Ctrl-C mid-wizard aborts non-zero under `set -eu` — never a half-written `~/.fah`; non-TTY runs print guidance and exit 1.
- Shell-less hosts SKIP their IT cases with named reasons; the CI job installs dash + busybox on ubuntu first (skip-not-fail, macOS pays nothing for dash).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart test/site/installer_golden_test.dart
dart test test/integration/setup_wizard_portability_test.dart   # --tags integration
# live, on a terminal:
dash -c 'cat site/setup.sh | dash'
```

> Note: a bare full-suite run on a dev box shows failures in files this PR
> does not touch, all environment-shaped and reproduced on `origin/main`:
> `test/browser_ext/*` needs Chrome for Testing (CI runs them only in
> browser-ext.yml); the `headless_*` / `backend_mode` / `yolo_rm_*` CLI
> integration tests fail when the harness's own `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` /
> `FA_PROVIDER_*` env leaks into the spawned CLI (they pass with those vars
> unset); `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts in the pty2
> native layer at VM teardown after its 5 tests pass.

  S -->|curl | sh| DASH[dash / busybox ash / bash — pty IT]

```

#1596
### What changed
- Rebuilt the first-run wizard (`site/setup.sh`) as generator-rendered POSIX sh: `scripts/gen_installers.dart` now emits the provider/mode/approval menus from the live catalog, and the template dropped every bashism (`printf -v`, `read -p`, `read -s`) that crashed dash and silently corrupted busybox ash under `curl | sh` (#1596).
- New REG CI leg `installer-portability` (path-triggered on `site/**` + the generator): ubuntu runs dash + busybox ash, macOS runs bash; red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class.

### Key decisions
- Single source of truth: the `/model` TUI presets table (`lib/src/cli/model_presets.dart`, extracted from `provider_models.dart`) now feeds both the CLI menu and the installer menus — the provider/approval data no longer has a second copy in `install-config.yaml`.
- Hidden key entry uses `stty -echo` + by-name `read` (dash has no `read -s`); the key never rides `printf` argv (ps-safe) and is byte-scanned out of every test transcript.
- EOF/Ctrl-C mid-wizard aborts non-zero under `set -eu` — never a half-written `~/.fah`; non-TTY runs print guidance and exit 1.
- Shell-less hosts SKIP their IT cases with named reasons; the CI job installs dash + busybox on ubuntu first (skip-not-fail, macOS pays nothing for dash).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart test/site/installer_golden_test.dart
dart test test/integration/setup_wizard_portability_test.dart   # --tags integration
# live, on a terminal:
dash -c 'cat site/setup.sh | dash'
```

> Note: a bare full-suite run on a dev box shows failures in files this PR
> does not touch, all environment-shaped and reproduced on `origin/main`:
> `test/browser_ext/*` needs Chrome for Testing (CI runs them only in
> browser-ext.yml); the `headless_*` / `backend_mode` / `yolo_rm_*` CLI
> integration tests fail when the harness's own `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` /
> `FA_PROVIDER_*` env leaks into the spawned CLI (they pass with those vars
> unset); `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts in the pty2
> native layer at VM teardown after its 5 tests pass.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CAT[model_presets.dart — live catalog] --> GEN[gen_installers.dart]
  GEN --> T[setup.sh.template — POSIX sh]
  T --> S[site/setup.sh — golden-pinned bytes]
  S -->|curl | sh| DASH[dash / busybox ash / bash — pty IT]
  CI[installer-portability CI leg] -->|red| BLOCK[quality gate blocks merge]
```

</details>

#1596
### What changed
- Rebuilt the first-run wizard (`site/setup.sh`) as generator-rendered POSIX sh: `scripts/gen_installers.dart` now emits the provider/mode/approval menus from the live catalog, and the template dropped every bashism (`printf -v`, `read -p`, `read -s`) that crashed dash and silently corrupted busybox ash under `curl | sh` (#1596).
- New REG CI leg `installer-portability` (path-triggered on `site/**` + the generator): ubuntu runs dash + busybox ash, macOS runs bash; red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class.

### Key decisions
- Single source of truth: the `/model` TUI presets table (`lib/src/cli/model_presets.dart`, extracted from `provider_models.dart`) now feeds both the CLI menu and the installer menus — the provider/approval data no longer has a second copy in `install-config.yaml`.
- Hidden key entry uses `stty -echo` + by-name `read` (dash has no `read -s`); the key never rides `printf` argv (ps-safe) and is byte-scanned out of every test transcript.
- EOF/Ctrl-C mid-wizard aborts non-zero under `set -eu` — never a half-written `~/.fah`; non-TTY runs print guidance and exit 1.
- Shell-less hosts SKIP their IT cases with named reasons; the CI job installs dash + busybox on ubuntu first (skip-not-fail, macOS pays nothing for dash).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart test/site/installer_golden_test.dart
dart test test/integration/setup_wizard_portability_test.dart   # --tags integration
# live, on a terminal:
dash -c 'cat site/setup.sh | dash'
```

> Note: a bare full-suite run on a dev box shows failures in files this PR
> does not touch, all environment-shaped and reproduced on `origin/main`:
> `test/browser_ext/*` needs Chrome for Testing (CI runs them only in
> browser-ext.yml); the `headless_*` / `backend_mode` / `yolo_rm_*` CLI
> integration tests fail when the harness's own `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` /
> `FA_PROVIDER_*` env leaks into the spawned CLI (they pass with those vars
> unset); `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts in the pty2
> native layer at VM teardown after its 5 tests pass.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CAT[model_presets.dart — live catalog] --> GEN[gen_installers.dart]
  GEN --> T[setup.sh.template — POSIX sh]
  T --> S[site/setup.sh — golden-pinned bytes]
  S -->|curl | sh| DASH[dash / busybox ash / bash — pty IT]
  CI[installer-portability CI leg] -->|red| BLOCK[quality gate blocks merge]
```

</details>

### What changed
- Rebuilt the first-run wizard (`site/setup.sh`) as generator-rendered POSIX sh: `scripts/gen_installers.dart` now emits the provider/mode/approval menus from the live catalog, and the template dropped every bashism (`printf -v`, `read -p`, `read -s`) that crashed dash and silently corrupted busybox ash under `curl | sh` (#1596).
- New REG CI leg `installer-portability` (path-triggered on `site/**` + the generator): ubuntu runs dash + busybox ash, macOS runs bash; red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class.

### Key decisions
- Single source of truth: the `/model` TUI presets table (`lib/src/cli/model_presets.dart`, extracted from `provider_models.dart`) now feeds both the CLI menu and the installer menus — the provider/approval data no longer has a second copy in `install-config.yaml`.
- Hidden key entry uses `stty -echo` + by-name `read` (dash has no `read -s`); the key never rides `printf` argv (ps-safe) and is byte-scanned out of every test transcript.
- EOF/Ctrl-C mid-wizard aborts non-zero under `set -eu` — never a half-written `~/.fah`; non-TTY runs print guidance and exit 1.
- Shell-less hosts SKIP their IT cases with named reasons; the CI job installs dash + busybox on ubuntu first (skip-not-fail, macOS pays nothing for dash).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart test/site/installer_golden_test.dart
dart test test/integration/setup_wizard_portability_test.dart   # --tags integration
# live, on a terminal:
dash -c 'cat site/setup.sh | dash'
```

> does not touch, all environment-shaped and reproduced on `origin/main`:
> `test/browser_ext/*` needs Chrome for Testing (CI runs them only in
> browser-ext.yml); the `headless_*` / `backend_mode` / `yolo_rm_*` CLI
> integration tests fail when the harness's own `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` /
> `FA_PROVIDER_*` env leaks into the spawned CLI (they pass with those vars
> unset); `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts in the pty2
> native layer at VM teardown after its 5 tests pass.

flowchart TD

  S -->|curl | sh| DASH[dash / busybox ash / bash — pty IT]
  CI[installer-portability CI leg] -->|red| BLOCK[quality gate blocks merge]
```

#1596
### What changed
- Rebuilt the first-run wizard (`site/setup.sh`) as generator-rendered POSIX sh: `scripts/gen_installers.dart` now emits the provider/mode/approval menus from the live catalog, and the template dropped every bashism (`printf -v`, `read -p`, `read -s`) that crashed dash and silently corrupted busybox ash under `curl | sh` (#1596).
- New REG CI leg `installer-portability` (path-triggered on `site/**` + the generator): ubuntu runs dash + busybox ash, macOS runs bash; red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class.

### Key decisions
- Single source of truth: the `/model` TUI presets table (`lib/src/cli/model_presets.dart`, extracted from `provider_models.dart`) now feeds both the CLI menu and the installer menus — the provider/approval data no longer has a second copy in `install-config.yaml`.
- Hidden key entry uses `stty -echo` + by-name `read` (dash has no `read -s`); the key never rides `printf` argv (ps-safe) and is byte-scanned out of every test transcript.
- EOF/Ctrl-C mid-wizard aborts non-zero under `set -eu` — never a half-written `~/.fah`; non-TTY runs print guidance and exit 1.
- Shell-less hosts SKIP their IT cases with named reasons; the CI job installs dash + busybox on ubuntu first (skip-not-fail, macOS pays nothing for dash).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart test/site/installer_golden_test.dart
dart test test/integration/setup_wizard_portability_test.dart   # --tags integration
# live, on a terminal:
dash -c 'cat site/setup.sh | dash'
```

> Note: a bare full-suite run on a dev box shows failures in files this PR
> does not touch, all environment-shaped and reproduced on `origin/main`:
> `test/browser_ext/*` needs Chrome for Testing (CI runs them only in
> browser-ext.yml); the `headless_*` / `backend_mode` / `yolo_rm_*` CLI
> integration tests fail when the harness's own `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` /
> `FA_PROVIDER_*` env leaks into the spawned CLI (they pass with those vars
> unset); `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts in the pty2
> native layer at VM teardown after its 5 tests pass.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CAT[model_presets.dart — live catalog] --> GEN[gen_installers.dart]
  GEN --> T[setup.sh.template — POSIX sh]
  T --> S[site/setup.sh — golden-pinned bytes]
  S -->|curl | sh| DASH[dash / busybox ash / bash — pty IT]
  CI[installer-portability CI leg] -->|red| BLOCK[quality gate blocks merge]
```

</details>

### What changed
- Rebuilt the first-run wizard (`site/setup.sh`) as generator-rendered POSIX sh: `scripts/gen_installers.dart` now emits the provider/mode/approval menus from the live catalog, and the template dropped every bashism (`printf -v`, `read -p`, `read -s`) that crashed dash and silently corrupted busybox ash under `curl | sh` (#1596).
- New REG CI leg `installer-portability` (path-triggered on `site/**` + the generator): ubuntu runs dash + busybox ash, macOS runs bash; red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class.

### Key decisions
- Single source of truth: the `/model` TUI presets table (`lib/src/cli/model_presets.dart`, extracted from `provider_models.dart`) now feeds both the CLI menu and the installer menus — the provider/approval data no longer has a second copy in `install-config.yaml`.
- Hidden key entry uses `stty -echo` + by-name `read` (dash has no `read -s`); the key never rides `printf` argv (ps-safe) and is byte-scanned out of every test transcript.
- EOF/Ctrl-C mid-wizard aborts non-zero under `set -eu` — never a half-written `~/.fah`; non-TTY runs print guidance and exit 1.
- Shell-less hosts SKIP their IT cases with named reasons; the CI job installs dash + busybox on ubuntu first (skip-not-fail, macOS pays nothing for dash).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart test/site/installer_golden_test.dart
dart test test/integration/setup_wizard_portability_test.dart   # --tags integration
# live, on a terminal:
dash -c 'cat site/setup.sh | dash'
```

> Note: a bare full-suite run on a dev box shows failures in files this PR
> does not touch, all environment-shaped and reproduced on `origin/main`:
> `test/browser_ext/*` needs Chrome for Testing (CI runs them only in
> browser-ext.yml); the `headless_*` / `backend_mode` / `yolo_rm_*` CLI
> integration tests fail when the harness's own `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` /
> `FA_PROVIDER_*` env leaks into the spawned CLI (they pass with those vars
> unset); `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts in the pty2
> native layer at VM teardown after its 5 tests pass.

  GEN --> T[setup.sh.template — POSIX sh]

### What changed
- Rebuilt the first-run wizard (`site/setup.sh`) as generator-rendered POSIX sh: `scripts/gen_installers.dart` now emits the provider/mode/approval menus from the live catalog, and the template dropped every bashism (`printf -v`, `read -p`, `read -s`) that crashed dash and silently corrupted busybox ash under `curl | sh` (#1596).
- New REG CI leg `installer-portability` (path-triggered on `site/**` + the generator): ubuntu runs dash + busybox ash, macOS runs bash; red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class.

### Key decisions
- Single source of truth: the `/model` TUI presets table (`lib/src/cli/model_presets.dart`, extracted from `provider_models.dart`) now feeds both the CLI menu and the installer menus — the provider/approval data no longer has a second copy in `install-config.yaml`.
- Hidden key entry uses `stty -echo` + by-name `read` (dash has no `read -s`); the key never rides `printf` argv (ps-safe) and is byte-scanned out of every test transcript.
- EOF/Ctrl-C mid-wizard aborts non-zero under `set -eu` — never a half-written `~/.fah`; non-TTY runs print guidance and exit 1.
- Shell-less hosts SKIP their IT cases with named reasons; the CI job installs dash + busybox on ubuntu first (skip-not-fail, macOS pays nothing for dash).

### How to verify
```bash

dart test test/integration/setup_wizard_portability_test.dart   # --tags integration
# live, on a terminal:
dash -c 'cat site/setup.sh | dash'
```

> integration tests fail when the harness's own `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` /

> native layer at VM teardown after its 5 tests pass.

```

{"content":"# Fixed — temp config is `mktemp`-created (no predictable path)

The wizard's atomic config write no longer goes through a fixed,
symlink-followable name. `site/setup.sh.template` now reads:

```sh
mkdir -p "$FAH_CONFIG_DIR"
# mktemp, not a fixed name (gh-1596 review hardening): a predictable path
# like `.config.yaml.tmp` is symlink-followable — a pre-planted link there
# would redirect the write. The XXXXXX template form is supported by GNU,
# busybox and BSD mktemp alike; mktemp creates the file 0600, so the config
# lands owner-only (same-dir tmp keeps the mv atomic).
FAH_TMP_CONF=$(mktemp "$FAH_CONFIG_DIR/.config.yaml.XXXXXX")
```

- `site/setup.sh` regenerated from the template (golden-pinned bytes), so the
  shipped artifact carries the hardening.
- The EXIT-trap cleanup is untouched and still works: `mktemp` returns an
  existing path, `rm -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF"` remains a no-op after the successful
  `mv`, and under `set -eu` a failing `mktemp` aborts before any write.
- Done RED→GREEN per TDD: new regression tests
  (`UT-1b — temp-file hygiene` in `test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart`)
  assert every sh artifact assigns temp files only through `mktemp "<…XXXXXX>"`
  and never through a fixed `*.tmp` path — both setup artifacts failed before
  the fix and pass after; `site/install.sh`'s existing mktemp usage is covered
  by the same tests.
- The dash + busybox ash + bash pty integration flows (which execute this
  exact write path, including the Ctrl-C/EOF no-half-written-config edges)
  all pass on the fixed tree.

#1596
### What changed
- Rebuilt the first-run wizard (`site/setup.sh`) as generator-rendered POSIX sh: `scripts/gen_installers.dart` now emits the provider/mode/approval menus from the live catalog, and the template dropped every bashism (`printf -v`, `read -p`, `read -s`) that crashed dash and silently corrupted busybox ash under `curl | sh` (#1596).
- New REG CI leg `installer-portability` (path-triggered on `site/**` + the generator): ubuntu runs dash + busybox ash, macOS runs bash; red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class.

### Key decisions
- Single source of truth: the `/model` TUI presets table (`lib/src/cli/model_presets.dart`, extracted from `provider_models.dart`) now feeds both the CLI menu and the installer menus — the provider/approval data no longer has a second copy in `install-config.yaml`.
- Hidden key entry uses `stty -echo` + by-name `read` (dash has no `read -s`); the key never rides `printf` argv (ps-safe) and is byte-scanned out of every test transcript.
- EOF/Ctrl-C mid-wizard aborts non-zero under `set -eu` — never a half-written `~/.fah`; non-TTY runs print guidance and exit 1.
- Shell-less hosts SKIP their IT cases with named reasons; the CI job installs dash + busybox on ubuntu first (skip-not-fail, macOS pays nothing for dash).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart test/site/installer_golden_test.dart
dart test test/integration/setup_wizard_portability_test.dart   # --tags integration
# live, on a terminal:
dash -c 'cat site/setup.sh | dash'
```

> Note: a bare full-suite run on a dev box shows failures in files this PR
> does not touch, all environment-shaped and reproduced on `origin/main`:
> `test/browser_ext/*` needs Chrome for Testing (CI runs them only in
> browser-ext.yml); the `headless_*` / `backend_mode` / `yolo_rm_*` CLI
> integration tests fail when the harness's own `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` /
> `FA_PROVIDER_*` env leaks into the spawned CLI (they pass with those vars
> unset); `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts in the pty2
> native layer at VM teardown after its 5 tests pass.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CAT[model_presets.dart — live catalog] --> GEN[gen_installers.dart]
  GEN --> T[setup.sh.template — POSIX sh]
  T --> S[site/setup.sh — golden-pinned bytes]
  S -->|curl | sh| DASH[dash / busybox ash / bash — pty IT]
  CI[installer-portability CI leg] -->|red| BLOCK[quality gate blocks merge]
```

</details>

{"content":"# Fixed — temp config is `mktemp`-created (no predictable path)

The wizard's atomic config write no longer goes through a fixed,
symlink-followable name. `site/setup.sh.template` now reads:

```sh
mkdir -p "$FAH_CONFIG_DIR"
# mktemp, not a fixed name (gh-1596 review hardening): a predictable path
# like `.config.yaml.tmp` is symlink-followable — a pre-planted link there
# would redirect the write. The XXXXXX template form is supported by GNU,
# busybox and BSD mktemp alike; mktemp creates the file 0600, so the config
# lands owner-only (same-dir tmp keeps the mv atomic).
FAH_TMP_CONF=$(mktemp "$FAH_CONFIG_DIR/.config.yaml.XXXXXX")
```

- `site/setup.sh` regenerated from the template (golden-pinned bytes), so the
  shipped artifact carries the hardening.
- The EXIT-trap cleanup is untouched and still works: `mktemp` returns an
  existing path, `rm -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF"` remains a no-op after the successful
  `mv`, and under `set -eu` a failing `mktemp` aborts before any write.
- Done RED→GREEN per TDD: new regression tests
  (`UT-1b — temp-file hygiene` in `test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart`)
  assert every sh artifact assigns temp files only through `mktemp "<…XXXXXX>"`
  and never through a fixed `*.tmp` path — both setup artifacts failed before
  the fix and pass after; `site/install.sh`'s existing mktemp usage is covered
  by the same tests.
- The dash + busybox ash + bash pty integration flows (which execute this
  exact write path, including the Ctrl-C/EOF no-half-written-config edges)
  all pass on the fixed tree.

#1596
### What changed
- Rebuilt the first-run wizard (`site/setup.sh`) as generator-rendered POSIX sh: `scripts/gen_installers.dart` now emits the provider/mode/approval menus from the live catalog, and the template dropped every bashism (`printf -v`, `read -p`, `read -s`) that crashed dash and silently corrupted busybox ash under `curl | sh` (#1596).
- New REG CI leg `installer-portability` (path-triggered on `site/**` + the generator): ubuntu runs dash + busybox ash, macOS runs bash; red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class.

### Key decisions
- Single source of truth: the `/model` TUI presets table (`lib/src/cli/model_presets.dart`, extracted from `provider_models.dart`) now feeds both the CLI menu and the installer menus — the provider/approval data no longer has a second copy in `install-config.yaml`.
- Hidden key entry uses `stty -echo` + by-name `read` (dash has no `read -s`); the key never rides `printf` argv (ps-safe) and is byte-scanned out of every test transcript.
- EOF/Ctrl-C mid-wizard aborts non-zero under `set -eu` — never a half-written `~/.fah`; non-TTY runs print guidance and exit 1.
- Shell-less hosts SKIP their IT cases with named reasons; the CI job installs dash + busybox on ubuntu first (skip-not-fail, macOS pays nothing for dash).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart test/site/installer_golden_test.dart
dart test test/integration/setup_wizard_portability_test.dart   # --tags integration
# live, on a terminal:
dash -c 'cat site/setup.sh | dash'
```

> Note: a bare full-suite run on a dev box shows failures in files this PR
> does not touch, all environment-shaped and reproduced on `origin/main`:
> `test/browser_ext/*` needs Chrome for Testing (CI runs them only in
> browser-ext.yml); the `headless_*` / `backend_mode` / `yolo_rm_*` CLI
> integration tests fail when the harness's own `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` /
> `FA_PROVIDER_*` env leaks into the spawned CLI (they pass with those vars
> unset); `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts in the pty2
> native layer at VM teardown after its 5 tests pass.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD

  GEN --> T[setup.sh.template — POSIX sh]
  T --> S[site/setup.sh — golden-pinned bytes]
  S -->|curl | sh| DASH[dash / busybox ash / bash — pty IT]
  CI[installer-portability CI leg] -->|red| BLOCK[quality gate blocks merge]
```

</details>

{"content":"# Fixed — temp config is `mktemp`-created (no predictable path)

The wizard's atomic config write no longer goes through a fixed,
symlink-followable name. `site/setup.sh.template` now reads:

```sh

# busybox and BSD mktemp alike; mktemp creates the file 0600, so the config
